sources.entry: NeatPaste - Clean, lightweight native clipboard manager for macOS. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/NeatMacApps/NeatPaste) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: NeatPaste is a native macOS clipboard history manager that lives in the menu bar and pastes past text or images back into the app you're typing in.
summary.what_it_does: NeatPaste runs in the macOS menu bar and records what you copy into a local history. Pressing ⌘⌥V (or clicking the menu bar icon) opens a panel where you can type to filter items, move with arrow keys, and press Enter to paste into the current app. Space opens Quick Look for a preview. It stores both text and images, shows image thumbnails inline, and merges duplicate copies so the latest one moves to the top. History is kept for 7 days and persists across restarts, stored only on the Mac with no account, sync, or network use. The panel appears near the text cursor. Automatic paste requires Accessibility permission; without it, the item is copied to the system clipboard for manual ⌘V. The README also lists pinning, favorites, cloud sync, and AI as out of scope.
use_cases: recall text copied earlier in the day
paste an older copied image into a document
keep clipboard history private on a Mac
paste without reaching for the mouse
filter past clipboard entries by typing
manage repeated copy-paste workflows in the menu bar
how_to_run: Or download the signed and notarized NeatPaste-x.y.z.dmg from the releases page and drag it to /Applications
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd NeatPaste, run xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -project NeatPaste.xcodeproj -scheme NeatPaste -configuration Release -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData build
Copy build/DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/NeatPaste.app to /Applications and open it, then press ⌘⌥V
notable: Stays fully local: no account, no sync, no network access per the README
Keeps rich content such as images without downgrading to plain text
Panel opens next to the text cursor and supports Quick Look previews
Falls back to copying to the system clipboard when Accessibility permission is not granted
Signed and notarized DMG plus a Homebrew cask install path
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon
README lists no pinning, favorites, cloud sync, App Store build, or other platforms
Settings mention ignored apps as 'coming next', so that feature is not yet available
